setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. The Scale page is open on the transposition fader along the bottom row. Global transposition is +4 (set at (13,8)). Scale-track step 2 has a transposition lock of 0, the fader's centre at (12,8), and step 1 has a lock of -12, the lowest value at (9,8). The MIDI strip reads 48, 62, 64, 65: step 1 sounds an octave below its written note, while steps 2 to 4 ignore the global +4 because the zero lock on step 2 holds for the rest of the loop. This is how you keep one part of a song at its written pitch while the rest is transposed.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press the right end of the fader, (16,8), twelve times, playing as you go if you like. Each press adds one semitone, from -12 up to 0. A lock of 0 is an explicit lock: it overrides the global +4, so step 1 plays MIDI 60 and not 64.
steps.title: Walk step 1 up to an explicit zero

steps.caption: Keep holding step 1 and press (16,8) twelve more times. Each press adds one semitone, up to +12. The first note jumps an octave to MIDI 72. Steps 2 to 4 still follow the zero lock on step 2 and stay at MIDI 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Walk on up to +12

steps.caption: Hold scale-track step 1 and press K2 to remove its lock. Step 1 now follows the global +4 and plays MIDI 64. The zero lock on step 2 is still active for steps 2 to 4, so the loop plays MIDI 64, 62, 64 and 65.
steps.title: Clear the lock on step 1

title: Lock transposition without losing the global setting
